label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Hi Tolu, I’m Amaka_Bio100. I’m in Biology 100L now, and Medicine was my first choice too. I scored 251 in JAMB last year, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and was offered Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. So I know that portal-checking heartbreak. I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. My mum kept telling people in church I was doing Medicine for about two months until I begged her to stop. I’m telling you that because your disappointment is real; you don’t have to pretend you’re fine just because you got an offer.

About transferring: it is possible at my school, but please don’t treat it as guaranteed. Our level adviser said you need at least a 4.5 CGPA out of 5.0, and there has to be space in Medicine. She said about six people transferred in from the whole faculty last year, while she thought more than 40 applied. She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so a JAMB score of 268 by itself doesn’t tell us whether you qualify.

I’m still trying myself. After first semester, my CGPA is 4.31, so I haven’t reached 4.5. The first-year courses include BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones giving people a hard time, so it’s not simply “just read hard.” You’d need to find out what the workload and grading are like at your own school, too.

And there are extra costs: my lab coat was ₦6,500, my dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual cost extra. I’m sharing that so you have a more realistic picture, not to put you off.

Biology itself isn’t a bad course. I expected to be counting down the days until I could leave, but I’m enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I thought I would. During our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted; I was fine. That day I realised I actually like this kind of work. I still want to see where I can go from here, but I’m not miserable every day in Biology.

I also don’t want to pretend that taking the offer and rewriting are equally easy choices. Staying home for a year can be hard, and rewriting JAMB is not wrong if you’re ready to do it. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to try again for Medicine. She has written JAMB twice more and is still at home. That’s her situation, not a prediction of yours, but it’s worth thinking about when you weigh the options.

So Kingsley is wrong to say transfer is a myth, but Favour makes it sound too simple when she says you can just read hard. Transfer exists, but it’s competitive and depends on the rules and available spaces at your school. Please go to the faculty or department and ask for the exact transfer requirements for your own case—especially the CGPA, JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, timing, and whether Biology students are eligible. Don’t rely only on forum replies, including mine; the rules can differ from school to school.

One question I’d ask yourself is whether you want Medicine for the work itself, or because your parents and other people expect you to become a doctor. There’s no shame in wanting Medicine, and there’s no shame in choosing Biology if you find you genuinely like it. Just don’t accept Biology on the assumption that transfer is automatic, and don’t rewrite because people make it sound like the only respectable option.

Whatever you choose, it’s a hard decision, but it isn’t the end of the world. You don’t have to decide based on panic or other people’s certainty. Get the official requirements, talk it through with someone you trust, and choose the risk you feel most prepared to take.
